sites.rationale: DRD3 has no signal peptide in the canonical sequence; the N-terminus (residues 1–31) is the sole extracellular terminus, so any N-terminal tag must be prepended before M1 (insert_after_residue=0). No paper in the ledger names a specific junction residue, but the topology leaves exactly one extracellular terminus, making the position topology-derived rather than inferred. L5 provides the clearest surface-confirmation evidence (non-permeabilized cell immunofluorescence), and the same N-terminal tagging strategy is independently corroborated by L1 (HA), L3/L4 (VSV-SNAP, htrFRET surface confirmation), L7 (SNAP), and L8 (FLAG in neurons). Full-length human D3R with N-terminal cleavable HA signal peptide followed by FLAG (DYKDDDDK) expressed in HEK293T cells; Gly-9 and Ser-9 polymorphic variants both tested. Surface FLAG immunoreactivity detected on non-permeabilized cells, confirming extracellular display of the tag.

sources.claim: D) Surface FLAG immunoreactivity on HEK293T cells expressing the FLAG-tagged Gly-9 or Ser-9 D 3 R–NP constructs.

literature_notes: All eight ledger lines (L1–L8) support N-terminal tagging of full-length, membrane-anchored DRD3; none names a specific residue number for the junction. Because DRD3 has no endogenous signal peptide and the N-terminus (1–31) is the sole extracellular terminus, the position is unambiguously topology-derived at insert_after_residue=0. Several constructs (L3, L5/L6) prepend an exogenous signal peptide upstream of the tag to boost surface trafficking; the tag itself is still placed before native M1. No ledger line reports a tag insertion in ECL1 (89–103), ECL2 (171–187), or ECL3 (352–365), so no internal sites are proposed. The C-terminal Venus (L2) and NP tag (L6) land in the intracellular C-terminus (residues 387–400) and are recorded in other_positions.

literature_other_positions.note: C-terminal Venus fluorescent protein fused to full-length D3R; the C-terminus (residues 387–400) is intracellular per topology, so this tag faces the cytoplasm and is not a surface-display site.
C-terminal NP tag (GVTGWRLCERILA) with linker fused to full-length D3R-NP construct; C-terminus is intracellular, so this tag is cytoplasmic and not suitable for extracellular surface labelling.
